To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spectral nudging technique is a promising method to improve the simulation of TCs in regional climate models, but that further studies with different spectral nudging parameters and different regions are necessary in order to draw a general conclusion.

spectral nudging improves the simulation of typhoons in a regional climate model by reducing ensemble spread, by increasing pattern correlations, and by improving biases and root mean square errors of simulated fields.

spectral nudging reduces the number of simulated typhoons, but the number of simulated tracks which are similar with observed best tracks is increased and the tracks merge after a shorter time and follow the observed tracks closely; also the ensemble spread, root mean square errors, and biases of simulated fields are reduced and the pattern correlations are increased.
